doc: A tree species: everything that makes a pine a pine. Genomes are data (the workspace's config/tree_genomes/), shared by every tree system so the species, age, and season stay consistent between skeleton, body, and colour.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Display name, e.g. Pine.

fields.name: latin
fields.doc: Botanical name, for reference.

fields.name: excurrent
fields.doc: Strong apical dominance: the stem runs to the top (pine, hickory, ebony). Otherwise decurrent: the stem gives way to leaders in the crown (oak, apple).

fields.name: deciduous
fields.doc: Drops its leaves for winter.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Mature height in the game, metres. Game heights sit below wild ones so trees frame a hex map without hiding it (hero 1.8 m).

fields.name: slender
fields.doc: Height over trunk diameter of an open-grown mature tree (Pretzsch 2009); lower is stockier.

fields.name: trunk_diameter
fields.doc: Diameter of a mature tree's trunk at the ground, metres, from nature (before any swell or flare). It sets the trunk's width, the stump's collision, and the footprint (design/systems.md, Trees).

fields.name: crown_ratio
fields.doc: Live crown length over height: where branches start.

fields.name: crown_shape
fields.doc: Envelope of first-order branch lengths along the stem (Weber and Penn 1995).

fields.name: lean
fields.doc: Largest random lean of the trunk, radians.

fields.name: twist
fields.doc: Gnarliness of the trunk: random turn per segment, radians.

fields.name: flare
fields.doc: Root flare: how much wider the base is than the pipe model gives (0 = none).

fields.name: branches
fields.doc: First-order branches on the stem of a mature tree.

fields.name: branch_angle
fields.doc: First-order angle from the stem, degrees.

fields.name: branch_angle_var
fields.doc: Random spread of that angle, degrees.

fields.name: branch_length
fields.doc: Longest first-order branch over stem length.

fields.name: whorl
fields.doc: Branches per whorl (pines grow tiers); 0 = one at a time on a spiral.

fields.name: divergence
fields.doc: Turn between successive branches or whorls around the stem, degrees (137.5 is the golden angle).

fields.name: branch_curve
fields.doc: Bend over a first-order branch, radians: positive turns up, negative droops.

fields.name: tip_up
fields.doc: Extra upturn concentrated near branch tips, radians.

fields.name: twigs
fields.doc: Second-order branches on the longest first-order branch.

fields.name: twig_angle
fields.doc: Second-order angle from its parent, degrees.

fields.name: twig_length
fields.doc: Second-order length over its parent's length.

fields.name: twig_curve
fields.doc: Bend over a second-order branch, radians.

fields.name: sprigs
fields.doc: Third-order branches per second-order branch.

fields.name: sprig_length
fields.doc: Third-order length over its parent's length.

fields.name: cluster
fields.doc: Pushes children toward their parent's tip (0 = spread along, 1 = all at the tip); high values give the forking umbrella of a dragon tree.

fields.name: wobble
fields.doc: Gnarliness of branches: random turn per segment, radians.

fields.name: foliage
fields.doc: How foliage is built: broadleaf clumps (displaced icospheres), needle tufts (cones around the tips), rosettes, or palm fronds (pinnate leaflets along each first-order limb, which then carry no clumps; fruit hangs in a cluster under the crown).

fields.name: clump
fields.doc: Foliage clump radius over mature height.

fields.name: leafiness
fields.doc: Foliage clumps per branch tip region; 1 is a normal crown.

fields.name: fall_drop
fields.doc: Share of leaves already fallen in fall.

fields.name: winter_keep
fields.doc: Share of dead leaves a deciduous tree keeps through winter (oaks hold theirs: marcescence).

fields.name: blossom
fields.doc: Spring blossom: share of foliage clumps that flower (0 = none).

fields.name: blossom_leaf
fields.doc: Share of leaves already out while it blossoms (cherries flower on bare wood).

fields.name: fruit
fields.doc: Fruit (or cones) per foliage clump in the seasons it bears (0 = none).

fields.name: fruit_size
fields.doc: Fruit radius, metres (style.md section 3 wants it chunky).

fields.name: fruit_seasons
fields.doc: How ripe the fruit is per season (winter, spring, summer, fall; 4 values): 0 none, then unripe (just above 0) to ripe (1). Cones and pods that stay on the tree are fruit here too.

fields.name: pickable
fields.doc: Its fruit can be picked: the pipeline's fruit parameter applies, and the game can offer picking. Otherwise the parameter is disabled and whatever it bears (cones, propagules, seed pods) stays on.

fields.name: bark
fields.doc: Bark relief and pattern: ringed is a palm's leaf-scar rings; papery is a birch's pale bark with dark lenticel dashes and patches.

fields.name: dead_limbs
fields.doc: Share of first-order limbs that are dead and bare on an ancient tree.

fields.name: snow
fields.doc: How much snow settles on it in winter (0 for tropical trees).

fields.name: swell
fields.doc: Swollen lower trunk, as on water tupelo and bald cypress: how much wider the bottom quarter of the stem grows, tapering up (0 = none).

fields.name: knees
fields.doc: Cypress knees: woody cones rising from the roots around the trunk of a mature tree (0 = none).

fields.name: prop_roots
fields.doc: Prop roots: arching roots from the lower trunk down into the ground, as on a red mangrove (0 = none).

fields.name: hanging_moss
fields.doc: Spanish moss (an epiphyte) hanging in strands from the limbs, in every season (0 = none).

fields.name: moss_color
fields.doc: Colour of the hanging moss, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: age_height
fields.doc: Height of a sapling, young, mature, and ancient tree, as fractions of the mature height (4 values).

fields.name: age_girth
fields.doc: Trunk thickness multiplier for each age (4 values), on top of slenderness.

fields.name: flex
fields.doc: Wind flexibility: willows flutter, oaks are stiff.

fields.name: density
fields.doc: Green wood specific gravity (Wood Handbook): heavier wood falls harder and sways slower.

fields.name: stiffness
fields.doc: Green modulus of elasticity, GPa (Wood Handbook).

fields.name: bark_light
fields.doc: Bark colour on ridges, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: bark_dark
fields.doc: Bark colour in furrows, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: wood
fields.doc: Heartwood colour for cut and broken faces, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: leaf_spring
fields.doc: Leaf colour in spring, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: leaf_summer
fields.doc: Leaf colour in summer, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: leaf_fall
fields.doc: Leaf colour in fall, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: leaf_fall_alt
fields.doc: Second fall colour, mixed in per clump for variety, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: leaf_winter
fields.doc: Leaf colour in winter: an evergreen's winter tint, or a deciduous tree's dead leaves, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: blossom_color
fields.doc: Blossom colour, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: fruit_unripe
fields.doc: Fruit colour in summer, sRGB 0..1.

fields.name: fruit_ripe
fields.doc: Fruit colour in fall, sRGB 0..1.
